claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a single-phase fcc solid solution.
Adding Ti to the Co-Cr-Fe-Ni system modifies the stacking-fault energy.
The Ti-induced change in stacking-fault energy suppresses deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation in CoCrFeNiTi.
A related alloy, CrCoNi, undergoes a deformation-associated fcc-to-hcp transformation.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi is triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
Suppressing the fcc-to-hcp transformation causes plastic flow in CoCrFeNiTi to be dominated by facile dislocation glide.
Suppression of transformation leaves fewer impediments to dislocation motion in CoCrFeNiTi.
Facile dislocation glide produces minimal work hardening in CoCrFeNiTi.
Transformation suppression and limited work hardening account for the relatively low hardness and strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed glide-dominated mechanism retains favorable ductility in CoCrFeNiTi.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi provides increased strength without compromising plastic deformation.
Deformation-induced hcp regions strengthen alloys by nucleating obstacles to dislocation motion.
CoCrFeNiTi lacks an alternative strengthening mechanism such as transformation-induced plasticity or nanostructure formation at dislocation intersections.
Under identical deformation conditions, CoCrFeNiTi will have lower yield strength than a comparable Ti-free alloy that transforms to hcp.
Under identical deformation conditions, CoCrFeNiTi will have lower hardness than a comparable Ti-free alloy that transforms to hcp.
Deformed CoCrFeNiTi will remain predominantly fcc and develop little or no hcp phase.
Deformed CoCrFeNiTi will store fewer dislocations than the transforming reference alloy.
CoCrFeNi is an appropriate transforming reference expected to develop hcp during strain.
The proposed mechanism applies to well-annealed bulk CoCrFeNiTi tested from cryogenic temperature to room temperature at strain rates of 10^-3 to 10^-1 s^-1.
Diffusion is negligible in CoCrFeNiTi over the stated cryogenic-to-room-temperature deformation range.
